A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods and central experiments. Text extraction and rendered-page checks support comparison of the main text, equations, tables and Appendices A–E, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original Shakespeare experiments, OpenWebText model training and evaluation, ablations, timing measurements and finite-state simulations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds synthetic bound-tightness experiments, mask-count sensitivity tests and learned-cost experiments in Appendices C.5 and C.8.

M1.justification: Appendix C.8 adds an alternative OT cost based on the negative summed log probabilities of target tokens predicted from the source at t=0 (Equation 179). This changes coupling selection for the tested variant. The core DFM/MMF architecture, EMA mechanism and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds fixed-bigram synthetic sequence distributions, extending the original two-token, two-position examples to larger vocabularies and longer correlated sequences. The natural-language corpus and benchmark coverage remain unchanged; the new OpenWebText holdout is a split within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.9, Table 24 adds continuous-diffusion PLAID to the existing DFM-N, SEDD and GPT-2 comparison on the same five benchmarks at length 1024. PLAID scores are explicitly taken from Lou et al. (2024). The OT-to-Sinkhorn renaming elsewhere does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 256 masks, a 98%/2% OpenWebText split, and a synthetic evaluation using a three-unit bottleneck MLP, enumeration of partially masked states and terminal-distribution estimation over a dense temporal grid. These are additional protocols; the established language-model training budgets and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v4's solver, batch-size and EMA analyses, v5 adds mask-count and learned-cost ablations in Appendix C.8. Appendix C.5 also tests how bound tightness changes with learned-transition error and increasing state-space complexity. These substantially extend the design choices and bound behavior examined experimentally.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly calculate the reported standard deviations over generated samples, rather than training runs. Existing uncertainty entries and simulation-based estimation practices are retained. v5 introduces no seed information, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v5 adds bound-tightness results, 256-mask and learned-cost results, and PLAID scores in Tables 13 and 19–24. Table 10 corrects five values to match Table 3, including DFM-B at 128 steps from 191.48 to 192.75. Table 4 revises estimated pure-flow times at batch sizes 2048/4096 from 1129/2010 to 1176/2305 seconds. The headline Table 3 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 already contains an exact cross-entropy expression in Appendix A.5. v5 formalizes and reformulates it as Theorem A.2, supplies a detailed proof in A.8, and derives learned-probability-ratio approximations and their connection to the masked-flow bound. Appendix A.7 additionally proves invariance of unmasked positions in multimask flows. The central OT theorem and two bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion now explicitly present the precise perplexity formula as a core contribution, although an exact expression already appeared in v4's appendix. The introduction also extends the 32-fold step-reduction wording to inference time. The central OT, perplexity-bound and multimask-performance claims otherwise remain stable.

C2.justification: v5 interprets weaker OT gains with 256 masks through the coarser source grid and discusses the learned cost's advantage at few generation steps versus its weaker longer-step performance. The expanded bound-tightness discussion explicitly limits the new experiment to small synthetic settings and explains why it cannot estimate tightness at language-model scale.

D1.justification: The new experiments disclose fixed-bigram data construction, the MLP's hidden dimension of 3, transition lookup-table construction, temporal-grid evaluation and the 98%/2% OpenWebText split. The established architecture, optimizer settings, hardware, training-time disclosures and code destination are retained.

R1.justification: Remark 3.4 adds Maas (2011) and Léonard (2016), distinguishing the paper's coupling-wise identity for convex-interpolant DFM from earlier graph-distance and density-dependent-mobility formulations. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate citations.

P1.justification: v5 relocates and expands OT background into Section 2.2, adds an intuitive explanation of Theorem 3.1, rewrites the ablation narrative and reorganizes the exact-perplexity derivation. It also standardizes dissimilarity terminology and Sinkhorn names. These are focused revisions within the retained overall document structure.

P2.justification: v5 adds tables for the new analyses and PLAID comparison, revises captions and dataset/solver labels, relocates main-text tables and places all three existing algorithms on one page. Earlier Tables 13–17 remain as Tables 14–18. The overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: v5 provides fuller derivations, tests previously unexplored mask-count and cost-function choices, clarifies its relationship to earlier discrete OT work, and resolves five inconsistencies between Tables 3 and 10. These improve support and clarity incrementally. The headline experiments remain stable, and the added bound-tightness evidence is explicitly restricted to small synthetic settings.
